Submission s2 is graded and written to `grades/0001-s2.json`. It has 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only outputs a structured tool request. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You chose "it will eventually fix the bug". A repeating failure never ends by itself, so the program needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is right, but your reason, that the model runs each tool, is wrong. The model only requests tools and the program runs them. |
| q5 | correct | You covered both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | The name is part of it, but the model chooses from the full description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**What you have down:** the loop itself, that the model's output is a request, and what happens to a tool result.

**Work on next:** the split between what the model does and what the program does. The program runs the tools and ends the loop. The model chooses from full tool descriptions, which matters because you will write those for the makerspace tools.

**Next step:** reread the agent-loop and tool-use parts of "Building effective agents" (https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents). Then trace the laser-cutter question and mark each step as "model" or "program".

The workspace had no lessons, cheat sheets or sources, so I ran one web search. Only that Anthropic article came back as a usable source, and I couldn't read it in full. The feedback points to the article as a whole, not to named sections. I noted the gap in `RESOURCES.md`: I still need a primary page on tool-call mechanics and tool descriptions.

I also added learning record `0003` and updated `NOTES.md`. s1 is still ungraded.
